newsitem.title: SPAIN: Gas Natural sets model for Spanish privatisations.
newsitem.headline: Gas Natural sets model for Spanish privatisations.

text.p: The new Spanish government's ambitious privatisation programme has got off to a robust start as investors devoured a share offer for a 3.81 percent stake of energy group Gas Natural.
The Gas Natural sale was oversubscribed by more than three times the number of shares offered, state holding company SEPI said in a statement.
The group fixed a final price of 26,000 pesetas per share for the placement, up sharply from 23,000 pesetas at the start of the offer period, it said.
The shares' warm reception boded well for the six-month-old government's punishing privatisation schedule.

The Popular Party government, which this spring replaced the Socialists after 13 years of rule, announced in October an aggressive plan to privatise those groups still in state hands after partial sales by the Socialists.
The success of this sale appeared to lay to rest initial analysts' worries that the bourse would be unable to cope with the volumes the government was proposing.

"The price at which the (Gas Natural) stake was allocated shows the very high interest in these kind of (placements) and with Telefonica, Repsol and Endesa coming up, it indicates that the potential is massive," said Miguel Olabarri, head of research at Credit Lyonnais Securities in Madrid.
The Gas Natural sale will be followed by 21 percent of Telefonica at the start of 1997, and an initial public share offering for second telephone operator Retevision.
The government then plans to sell 10 percent of petrochemicals group Repsol, and a first slice of the state's remaining 66 percent of electricity giant Endesa, set for the second half of 1997.
Stakes in gas group Enagas, tobacco group Tabacalera and airport retail managers Aldeasa are also on the horizon, although the government has not yet set specific dates.
Telefonica, the next candidate on the agenda, has seen strong demand in the run-up. The stock has climbed from 1,690 pesetas on January 2 to a high of 2,885 pesetas on November 26.
The international appeal of Telefonica should make it a success despite the heavy schedule of international telecommunications flotations near the same time.
Germany's Deutsche Telekom came to market last month, and Italy's STET and France Telecom's, are expected next year.
For Gas Natural, the sale was aimed at institutional investors only, split 60-40 between domestic and international funds respectively.
Thus 854,112 shares of the total 1,423,5210 shares on offer will be allotted to Spanish institutions, with the remainder headed abroad.
